. It is submitted that appellants are innocent.
Victim has herself admitted that she did not know appellant Shankar Singh Marko.
She came to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:37436 3 CRA-573-2023 know about the name of appellant Shankar Singh Marko as was taken by co- accused/appellant Chotu Banjara.
It is submitted that in the FIR (Ex.P/2), name of the accused is mentioned as Chotu Banjara and name of Shankar Marco is not mentioned.
Victim has admitted in her cross examination that she was knowing the name of Shankar Singh Marko prior to lodging of an FIR.

Therefore, it is submitted that merely co-accused/appellant Chotu Banjara using premises of Appellant Shankar Singh Marku without the consent of Shankar Singh Marko will not make him an accused under Sections 366A, 342, or 368 of IPC.
It is submitted that none of the ingredients of Sections 366A, 342 and 368 of IPC are made out.
3 . It is submitted that as far as co-accused/appellant Chotu Banjara is concerned, it is a case of consent.

Mere positivity of the DNA report is not a sufficient circumstance to uphold conviction,
especially when Lady Dr. Usha Kiran (PW/8) stated that she had advised X-ray of right elbow, pelvis bones and knee joints for determination of the age of the victim and no such document is available on record.
In the light of the judgment of Supreme Court in Sunil Vs. State of Haryana (2010) 1 SCC 742 that will go against the prosecution as they have failed to prove the age of the victim.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the school teacher Mohan Singh Shyam (PW/18) admitted that though date of birth of the victim is mentioned as 10.05.2004 in Dakhil Kharid Register (Ex.P/24), but there is no indexing, no certification on the said register.
No basis is available on which date of birth of the victim was recorded.
He admitted that police had not asked for the admission form nor any birth certificate was sought.

There is no such document available on NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:37436 4 CRA-573-2023 record which may prove date of birth of the victim.

It is pointed out that father and mother of the victim too could not prove the date of birth and, therefore,
in absence of any documentary evidence to prove the date of birth of the victim, conviction as aforesaid cannot be upheld.
4 .
Shri Nitin Gupta, learned Government Advocate submits that DNA report (Ex.C/1) is positive qua Co-accused/appellant Chotu Banjara.
The age of the victim was about 14 years and, therefore at the time of the incident since she was about 14 and 1/2 years of age, her consent cannot be said to be a valid consent.
Hence, prays for dismissal of these appeals.

sentences.text:
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, victim (PW/1)
admitted in Para 10 of her cross-examination that she had heard name of appellant Shankar Singh Marko from co- accused/appellant Chotu Banjara.
She admitted that in her written complaint (Ex.P/1) that she had not mentioned the name of Shankar Singh Marko as landlord.
She admitted that prior to lodging of her report she already knew the name of Shankar Singh Marko.

6 . When these aspects are taken into consideration along with the fact that victim has also stated that she had run out of the house of Shankar meaning thereby that the gates of the house of Shankar were open and there was no illegal confinement.
Then coupled with the fact that victim stated that she had gone to the hospital when she was returning after examination then near Durga stage of Rajendragram, she was waiting for an Auto.

Co- accused/appellant Chotu Banjra deboarded the bus,
he threatened her and forcefully took her in the bus.
He took her to village-Bijora and later took NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:37436 5 CRA-573-2023 her to the house of Shankar Singh Marko, where in the night he committed wrong on two occasions.
She admitted that on the third day, she ran out of the house of Shankar to the road, boarded a bus, and came to her house.
When her parents returned then she had narrated the incident to them and then report was lodged.

Incident is said to be of 01.01.2019, whereas, FIR was lodged on 05.01.2019.
7 .
Thus, it is evident that provisions of Section 366A of IPC as far as appellant Shankar Singh Marko is concerned, will not be attracted, inasmuch as there is no element of procuration of minor girl.
There is no allegation of overt or covert act on the part of appellant Shankar Singh Marko.

Coupled with the fact that there is material omission as far as Appellant Shankar Singh Marko is concerned in the FIR (Ex.P/2), despite the admission that she knew the name of Shankar prior to the date of lodging of report.

As far as provisions of Section 342 of IPC are concerned, that too will not be made out because there is an admission of the victim that house of appellant Shankar Singh Marko was open, and she ran out of the house, boarded a bus, and came to her village.

Similarly, Section 368 of IPC deals with wrongfully concealing or keeping in confinement a kidnapped or abducted person,
too will not be applicable to the case of the appellant Shankar Singh Marko as none of the charge sections are available to uphold conviction of Shankar Singh Marko.
We have no hesitation to set aside his conviction.
Accordingly, his appeal CRA No.573/2023 is allowed.
His bail bonds be discharged.

8. As far as co-accused/appellant Chotu Banjara is concerned two NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:37436 6 CRA-573-2023 aspects are important.

One is that DNA report is pointing out towards his physical intimacy with the victim, but before resorting to conviction under Section 376 of IPC and under Section 5 r/w 6 of POCSO Act, it is to be examined as to whether victim was minor at the time of the incident.
Victim admitted in her cross examination that she used to visit Rajendragram every 6 month for her TB treatment.
She also admitted that there used to be discord in her house regarding expenditure of her treatment.
She has also admitted that when appellant Chotu Banjara took her to Village-Bijora she had no conversation with Shankar Singh Marko.
9 . Father of the victim (PW/2) stated that appellant Chotu Banjara is a Banjara community whereas Shankar Singh Marko is a 'Gond' community.
Victim is also from 'Gond' community.
Victim has studied up to 8th Class, thereafter she had left school.

It is stated that she studied at Government Chotu Banjara vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77830638/
3 School, Parcel Kala.

sentences.text: Mulahija of victim (Ex.P/24) reflects her date of birth to be 10.05.2004.
He has admitted in cross-examination that he has not prepared any horoscope for his daughter.
He also admitted that he is working as a Private Security Guard and due to his job, he usually remains outside his home.
He admitted that he has three daughters and victim used to visit hospital alone.
He has nowhere stated that victim was admitted by him in the school.

10. Ms.Dayavati Maravi, DSP (PW/3) admitted that victim had not informed her while giving her statements recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. that as to how appellant Chotu Banjara had threatened her.
She admitted that Rajendragram Bus stand has lot of population and victim
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:37436 7 CRA-573-2023 had not informed her as to she shouted for any help or not.
11. Mother of the victim (PW/5) stated that father of the victim had gone to the school for registering her name.
She further admitted that when she was admitted in first class then no documentary evidence was produced in support of date of birth of the victim.
She also admitted that prior to her admission in first class victim had studied at Aganwadi.

She admitted that victim had not informed her as to when the accused had forcefully made her to sit in the bus then whether she had cried for help or not, or had informed any co-passenger in the bus or not.
12. When this piece of evidence is taken into consideration along with the evidence of lady Dr. Usha Kiran (PW/8), who stated that there were no external or internal injury on the body of the victim.
Her hymen was old torn.
For determination the age of the victim, she had advised X- ray and there is no X-ray report on record coupled with the evidence of school teacher Mohan Singh Shyam (PW/18).
Then it is evident that prosecution has failed to prove that the victim was minor at the time of the incident.

13. Thus in the light of the judgment of Supreme Court in Sunil Vs. State of Haryana (2010) 1 SCC 742 when prosecution has failed to prove the age and it has also failed to conduct examinations by Dental Surgeon or Radiologist, inspite of being referred to for such examination by Dr. Usha Kiran (PW/8), age of the victim being doubtful as father of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:37436 8 CRA-573-2023 the victim has not said anything about date of birth or how the date of birth came to be recorded and there is no Anganwadi Certificate.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mother of the victim states that she had attended Anganwadi prior to the school.

The birth certificate on which lot of reliance is placed by Shri Nitin Gupta, learned Government Advocate, is not issued by any independent authority but by the same school i.e. School Teacher Mohan Singh Shyam (PW/18)
who has admitted that there was no documentary evidence as to the date of birth of the victim contained in (Ex.P/24), we are of the opinion that appellant Chotu Banjra is entitled to benefit of doubt.
14. Accordingly, impugned judgment of conviction and sentenced dated 16.12.2022 passed by learned Special Judge, POCSO Act, Annupur, is set aside.

The appellants, if not required in any,
other case, be set free Chotu Banjara vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77830638/
